output.name: Hirun
output.gloss: The Gull Who Flew the String

anatomy.part: the head, just above the breast
the peak of the left wing's leading edge
the trailing feather of the left wing
the bent feather at the right wing's wrist

output.myth: Hirun was the gull who flew the string for Mother Hesk. Each morning she carried the count from the islands up to the Reel at the pole, a wet grey bird with a bent foot and a temper worse than the weather. The day Aun took his knife to the string, Hirun was halfway up it. The cut came, and she was thrown out into Vel with her wings still open. Tavo laughed and would not take her down. She is up there yet, holding her wings wide as if the wind might change its mind. One tail feather is torn, so the two at the back do not match. Sil, searching for her brother, always stops to ask Hirun if she has seen him. Hirun says nothing. Gulls pass on only what they are given. If a gull kite comes back to you in the Reach, that is Hirun letting one message fall. Hesk keeps count of the gulls, and she is never short.
output.verse:
Hi-run holds out wings
wide into Tavo's cold breath
waiting for the reel

guess: A bird with spread wings, seen from the front, standing on thin legs
